notes: The dining room is the stage where the Major holds the table over the master's empty chair; the serving pantry behind the service door is the housekeeper's own ground, where the drawer and the sherry glass wait. The player will keep returning to the master's chair, the sideboard where the tureen changes hands, and the drawer in the pantry.

rooms.name: the dining room
rooms.description: A long room panelled in dark oak, with the mahogany table laid for twelve and the master's carver at its head beneath his own portrait. Two tall north windows give a flat grey light that never warms the cloth, and the marble chimneypiece draws badly, so the room smells of coal smoke, beeswax and old gravy. A sideboard runs the length of the inner wall under a row of covered dishes, and the floor creaks at the master's end where the boards have dried over the cellar.

rooms.name: the serving pantry
rooms.description: A narrow slip of a room behind the service door, shelved to the ceiling with the second-best china and the glass cloths folded in the housekeeper's own way. A lead sink under a small barred window, a scrubbed deal dresser with a locked drawer, and a plate-warmer that ticks as it cools. It smells of soda, damp cloth and the sherry nobody admits to drinking, and from here you can hear every word at the table through the service door.

exits.label: through the service door
exits.text: You put your shoulder to the service door and it swings on its silent hinge, the table's voices dropping to a murmur behind you.
exits.back_text: You ease the service door open an inch to listen, then step through into the smell of coal smoke and gravy.

objects.name: the master's chair
objects.description: The carver at the head of the table, its arms worn pale where he gripped them to rise. A fold of the cloth beside it is kept clear of plate, as though a place were still laid for a hand to rest on.

objects.name: the cloth
objects.description: Damask, double-laid, with the house crest woven at the master's end. A faint ring near the head, where something warm was set down without a mat, has not come out in two launderings.

objects.name: the sideboard
objects.description: Mahogany, long enough to stand four at once with their backs to the table. From here you can see every face at dinner in the mirror behind the covers, and nobody at the table thinks to look at you.

objects.name: the tureen
objects.description: The big Worcester soup tureen with the chipped lid, heavy enough to need two hands. Held out an instant too long, it hides whatever the mouth of the one holding it is doing.

objects.name: the carving set
objects.description: Horn-handled knife and fork in a baize-lined case on the sideboard. The master kept them sharp himself; the blade has a hair's turn at the point where he was careless once.

objects.name: the portrait
objects.description: The master at forty, hand on a dog that died before you came. The eyes are painted to follow the room, and from the sideboard they rest on his own empty chair.

objects.name: the grate
objects.description: A wide iron basket under the marble chimneypiece, with a fender that is kicked more than polished. The coal scuttle beside it is marked with the hour it was last filled, in Lavinia's chalk.

objects.name: the north windows
objects.description: Two tall sashes with the shutters folded back into the panelling. A line of gravel drive is just visible past the cedar, so whoever sits at the master's right sees the carriage before anyone else.

objects.name: the housekeeper's drawer
objects.description: The locked drawer of the deal dresser, the one key on your ring that has no label. It smells of wax and sherry when it opens, and the runners stick an inch from closed unless lifted just so.

objects.name: the sherry glass
objects.description: A small cut glass with a brown ring dried in the bowl and a smear on the rim the width of a lip. Unwashed, it still keeps an hour nobody has given you.

objects.name: the service door
objects.description: Green baize on the dining-room side, bare deal on this. It is hung to swing silently, and a servant standing with her ear a hand's breadth from it is invisible to the table.

objects.name: the lead sink
objects.description: A shallow lead trough under the barred window, with a brass tap that must be held open. Glasses are washed here last, and whoever washes them is the last to see what was in them.

objects.name: the plate-warmer
objects.description: A japanned tin cabinet on legs with a spirit lamp beneath, ticking as it cools. The lamp was lit for dinner the night the master died and nobody remembered to put it out.

objects.name: the glass cloths
objects.description: Linen cloths folded in thirds on the shelf, each marked in the corner with a stitched letter. One, with the previous housekeeper's initial, has been turned so the mark faces the wall.

objects.name: the tray
objects.description: The papier-mâché tea tray with the mother-of-pearl rose, the one Lavinia carries up and the one that comes back with a cup you did not ring for.
